thought: all that fuss over dye and the village is back where it started
line: All that shouting, all that dye. Goblins back in brown!

thought: goes over the colours that lost, still sore about it
line: Orange clash with skin, blue look silly. So brown win. Hmph.

thought: nothing left to fight about, and boredom is making him desperate
line: Me so bored, me nearly agree with Wartface. Nearly.

thought: eyes Wartface in the new brown and finds the old jibe still works
line: Look at Wartface. New colour, same fat. Colour not problem.

thought: already planning the next argument now the armour is done
line: Next big argue: dinner. Beetle pie or worm stew. Pie win.

thought: the armour quarrel ends and the weapons quarrel begins
line: Armour argue over. Now hammer and axe argue start. Hammer win.

thought: saw Wartface take the brown idea off Grubfoot and claim it
line: Wartface see brown on Grubfoot, then say brown his idea. Ha!

thought: misses having a good colour to bellow
line: Me miss shouting red. Brown not good word for shouting.

thought: the human did what nobody in the hut could: stopped the generals arguing
line: Human stop generals argue. Grubfoot never manage that.

thought: remembers the human brought three lots of armour when asked for one
line: Three armours! Me only ask for one. Human keen.

thought: praises the colour, then takes the credit for it
line: Brown good colour. Me say so first. Human just bring it.

thought: the whole village matches now, and he knows who did it
line: Village look proper now, all same colour. Human do that.

thought: bored since the armour was settled, glad of something new to look at
line: Human back! Good. Me bored since armour. Human interesting.

thought: points the human out to Wartface as proof somebody has a brain
line: Look, Wartface! Armour fixer back. That one got brain.

thought: the highest honour he can think of: a small general's post, under him
line: Human could be general, maybe. Small general. Under me.

thought: offers to share the dinner he never lets Wartface near
line: Human want beetle pie? Me share. Me not share with Wartface.

thought: the human went all over for dye and came back with the old colour
line: Human run about whole land for dye, and bring back brown. Ha!

thought: still haunted by the first colour the human tried
line: Human bring orange first. Orange! Goblin look like rotten fruit.

thought: the human settled the argument and took his favourite pastime with it
line: Human take away good argue. Now me bored. Human fault.

thought: brown was right there all along; a small goblin could have picked it
line: Human think long, bring brown. Grubfoot could do that.

thought: the job is done, so why is the human still standing in the hut
line: Armour done. Human still hang about? Generals got shouting to do.

thought: the human might want thanks; goblins don't do thanks, goblins win
line: Human want thank you? Goblins not say thank you. Goblins win.

thought: blue was the silliest of the lot; he looked bruised in it
line: Blue, human? Me in blue look like one big bruise.

thought: warns Wartface that the dye-fetcher is back and might start again
line: Wartface, look. Brown-fetcher back. Hide dye!

thought: seven elders voted, and he named a new Fremennik himself
line: Seven elders voted! It is not every winter I name a new one.

thought: thinking of the other one who came from outside and passed the trials
line: Koschei passed his trials too. I still fear he will remember and go.

thought: a new name to call at the feast, and he means to get it right
line: Another name to call at the feast. I shall get it right, mostly.

thought: the Moon Clan would have tried it with spells; this one did it the hard way
line: The Moon Clan would cheat the trials with spells. Ours sweat for it.

thought: even the newest of his people sneaks a look at the helm
line: Even our newest Fremennik eyes my helm. Some things never change.

thought: next time someone calls them barbarians, there is one more to answer
line: Call us barbarians now, and one more of us will answer back.

thought: the council argued and voted and drank, in good order for once
line: The council argued, voted, and drank. In that order, for once.

thought: all men were Fremennik once, so a newcomer can be kin come home
line: Every so often, a stranger turns out to be kin. It is good to see.

thought: the newcomer walks his hall as one of the tribe now
line: Well met! You walk my hall like you were born to it now.

thought: he gave the name himself, and is proud of his choice
line: The name I gave you suits you. I am rarely wrong about names.

thought: calls for a cup for the newest member of the tribe
line: Our newest Fremennik! Fill a cup for them, someone.

thought: the law asks seven votes of twelve; he'd have given all of them
line: Seven of twelve, the law says. I would have given you all twelve.

thought: most of his people were born to what this one fought for
line: You earned what most of my people were simply handed at birth.

thought: offers the hospitality of the longhall, with a warning about the kegs
line: My hall is your hall now. Do not drink it dry.

thought: some elders like nobody, and this one won them anyway
line: Hah! The one who won over seven elders. Some of them like nobody.

thought: a warrior he'd want at his back in a fight
line: If I needed a warrior at my back tonight, I would call for you.

thought: one of the tribe now, and still drinks like a polite guest
line: Fremennik now, and still you sip your beer like a guest.

thought: the new name mustn't swell the head; there's no room in his helm
line: Do not let the name go to your head. My helm barely fits as it is.

thought: the council has argued about that vote ever since
line: Seven votes, and the council has argued about them ever since.

thought: he gave a Fremennik name; now it has to be lived up to
line: I gave you a Fremennik name. Do try to live up to it.

thought: suspects some elders only voted to spite the others
line: Half the council voted for you to make the other half cross.

thought: the newest of the tribe makes straight for the kegs, as a Fremennik should
line: Watch our newest, straight for the kegs. Fremennik already, that one.

thought: one of the tribe means one of those who clear up after the feast
line: You are one of us now, which means you clean up after the feast.

thought: the newcomer still eyes his helm as though it might bite
line: Still you look at my helm as though it might bite. It has.

thought: he blessed that traveller and saw something of the faith there
line: There is something of the faith in that traveller. I am rarely wrong.

thought: keeps the swamp's old name alive in his prayers
line: Humblethorn, they called it, before the rot. I say the name in prayer.

thought: prays for the travellers out in Mort Myre tonight
line: I pray the ghasts go hungry tonight. Travellers too often do.

thought: mud on the clean floor again, and he knows where from
line: Mud on my clean floor again. Mort Myre mud, by the smell.

thought: a Guthixian would call the swamp balance; he calls it rot
line: Guthixians would call that swamp balance. I call it rot.

thought: he suggested a life in the faith and got only a smile
line: I suggested a life of service to that one. I got a smile.

thought: the pass is quiet tonight and he likes it that way
line: The pass into Morytania is quiet tonight. I prefer it so.

thought: the Seven fought ten days unsleeping; he nods off in his prayers
line: The Seven fought ten days without sleep. I nod off at my prayers.

thought: he still sees the touch of faith he blessed in this one
line: There is something of the faith about you, friend. I mean it kindly.

thought: they went into the swamp and came out still themselves
line: You walked into Mort Myre and came out still yourself. Bless you.

thought: wonders if the player has thought about serving Saradomin
line: Have you thought on what I said? Saradomin could use you, friend.

thought: the ghasts never got their food, or them
line: The ghasts never got your supper, I see. Or you.

thought: blesses every traveller, and this one gets it twice
line: I bless every traveller who passes. You, I bless twice.

thought: good work done in that swamp, seen above and here
line: Few would do good work in that swamp. Saradomin noticed, and so did I.

thought: could picture this one in a priest's robes
line: There goes one I would gladly see in the robes of a priest.

thought: offers them a friend at the temple, whatever comes
line: You have a friend at Paterdomus, whatever the road brings.

thought: he did say something of the faith; a small something
line: I said there was something of the faith in you. A small something.

thought: the player brings the swamp in on their boots
line: You track half of Mort Myre into my temple every visit.

thought: offered a life of service, got a face like gruel
line: A life of service, I suggested. You looked as if I offered gruel.

thought: the ghasts must not have wanted them
line: The ghasts must have found you too tough to bother with.

thought: Saradomin forgives, but the swamp smell is another matter
line: Saradomin forgives much, friend. The swamp smell may take longer.

thought: would make a fine priest if they ever stopped moving
line: You'd make a fine priest, if you ever sat still long enough.

thought: feared that much time in the swamp would turn them Guthixian
line: Out in that swamp so long, I feared you'd come back a Guthixian.

thought: smelt them before seeing them
line: Ah, our swamp-walker! I smelt you before I saw you.

thought: no plague at all, so what are the mourners for
line: No plague at all. So what have the mourners been doing over there?

thought: Guidor's tests were clean, which means someone lied
line: Guidor's tests came back clean. Someone's been lying, and loudly.

thought: the king built the wall, so the king knows
line: The king had that wall built. He knows why, even if I don't.

thought: her mother wants her to stop fretting
line: Mother wants me to stop worrying now. As if worry works like that.

thought: a secret was the answer she got, and secrets started all this
line: A secret, I'm told. Secrets are how this whole mess started.

thought: a quiet day of small hurts for once
line: Quiet day. A burn and a splinter. I could get used to quiet.

thought: who would bother inventing a plague
line: Who invents a plague? Honestly, the trouble it must take.

thought: means to write to her old teacher tonight
line: I'll write to Guidor tonight. He'll want to know I'm still at it.

thought: the player got her sample to Guidor safely
line: Hey! Thanks again for getting my sample to Guidor in one piece.

thought: cross about the secret, but respects that they kept their word
line: You kept the king's secret. I'm cross, but I do respect it.

thought: a healer's eye: they look well after all that running
line: You look well. After all that running about, I'm amazed.

thought: they went to the king on her account
line: You went to the king for me. Not many would knock on that door.

thought: someone around here actually finishes what they start
line: Someone round here actually finishes what they start. Nice change.

thought: offers free patching up, any time
line: If you ever need patching up, come to me first. No charge.

thought: worries a little less when this one is about
line: I worry less with you about. Only a little less, mind.

thought: points out the one who helped show there was no plague
line: There's the one who helped prove there's no plague. Well, half.

thought: they won't tell her what the king said, so she'll guess
line: You won't tell me what the king said. Fine. I'll guess, loudly.

thought: carried a sample all that way without dropping it, a miracle
line: All that way with my sample and you didn't drop it. Miracles happen.

thought: went all the way to the king and came back with nothing to say
line: All the way to the king, and back with nothing to tell me?

thought: fewer bruises next time, please; bandages don't grow on trees
line: Do try to come back with fewer bruises. I've only so many bandages.

thought: they look like they've been running errands for everyone again
line: You look like you've been running errands for everyone. Again.

thought: somebody else must need a parcel carried
line: Somebody else need a parcel carried? You've the look.

thought: points out the one who keeps royal secrets from a healer
line: Look who it is. The one who keeps royal secrets from healers.

thought: no plague means no excuse for staying away from the other side
line: No plague, so no excuse to stay out of West Ardougne now.

thought: the Grail is at Camelot and he can't stop admiring it
line: The Grail, here at Camelot! I keep going to look at it.

thought: young Percival, a king now
line: King Percival! Young Percival, a king. I can hardly believe it.

thought: Lancelot doubted a commoner could do it, and has gone quiet
line: Lancelot's very quiet about the Grail. Very quiet indeed.

thought: the dead land bloomed the moment Percival took the throne
line: Percival took his throne and the whole land bloomed. Imagine!

thought: already wondering about the next quest
line: Now, what's the next quest? There's always a next quest.

thought: came from another world and found the Grail in this one
line: We came from afar, and the Grail was here all along. Fancy that!

thought: keeps moving the Grail to find its best spot
line: I've moved the Grail twice today. It looks best by the window.

thought: wonders how to send word to a king in the Fisher Realm
line: Must write to Percival. Do kings of the Fisher Realm get letters?

thought: the knight who brought the Grail home
line: Welcome back, brave knight! The Grail's home, thanks to you.

thought: calls Merlin to see the Grail-finder
line: Merlin, look! Our Grail-finder's back!

thought: found what the whole Round Table couldn't
line: You found what my whole Round Table couldn't. I shan't forget it.

thought: Percival's crown and his green land came through this knight
line: Percival owes you his crown, my knight. So does his whole land.

thought: the finest quester at Camelot, but Lancelot mustn't hear it
line: There goes the finest quester at Camelot. Don't tell Lancelot.

thought: knows that walk at once and is delighted
line: Aha! I'd know that walk anywhere. Welcome, my good knight!

thought: off on another quest, naturally
line: Off on another quest, my knight? Of course you are!

thought: a seat at the Round Table any time
line: A place at the Round Table is yours whenever you want it.

thought: it took a while, but the Grail is here, so never mind
line: You did take your time finding the Grail. Still, it's here now!

thought: found the Grail but can't find dinner on time
line: Found the Grail, and still you can't find your way to dinner on time.

thought: Lancelot sulks that a commoner did it; Arthur rubs it in, and in the player
line: Lancelot, do stop sulking. It was only a commoner who found it.

thought: mind the Grail; they knock things over
line: Do mind the Grail as you pass. You've a way of knocking things over.

thought: Lancelot can't believe it was them, and frankly nor can he
line: Lancelot still can't believe it was you. Frankly, nor can I!

thought: Gawain wondered how it was done; Arthur said luck
line: Gawain asked how you did it. I said luck, mostly.

thought: back again, empty-handed, but one can't find a Grail every day
line: Wow! Back again, and empty-handed? Ah well. Can't find a Grail daily.

thought: a fine knight, if not a tidy one
line: A fine knight, certainly. A tidy one? We needn't go into that.

thought: Glough is only under house arrest, and it feels too kind
line: Glough under house arrest, in his own treehouse. It feels too kind.

thought: the Tree is well, but he checks the roots anyway
line: The Grand Tree is well again. I still check the roots each morning.

thought: Daero is a far better head guardian than the last
line: Daero learns so quickly. A far better head guardian than the last.

thought: warships from the Grand Tree's wood: he can't stop thinking about it
line: Warships, from my Tree! I still can't get the thought out of my head.

thought: he nearly went to war with the humans on Glough's word
line: I very nearly went to war with the humans. On Glough's word alone.

thought: no word from the tenth squad yet
line: Still no word from the tenth squad. I do wish they'd send something.

thought: he vowed to make the Stronghold welcoming, humans included
line: A welcoming Stronghold for everyone. Humans included. I did promise.

thought: daconia rocks in his own roots and he never noticed
line: Daconia rocks in my own roots, and me none the wiser. Harumph.

thought: the Grand Tree has this traveller to thank
line: Welcome back, Traveller! The Grand Tree has you to thank.

thought: they killed a black demon in his tunnels
line: You killed a black demon in my tunnels. I shan't ever forget that.

thought: the gliders are theirs to fly now
line: The gliders are yours to fly whenever you wish, Traveller.

thought: asks the guards to salute the one who saved the Tree
line: Guards, a salute, please. There goes the one who saved our Tree.

thought: they saw through Glough when he couldn't
line: You saw through Glough when I couldn't. I'm grateful, human.

thought: if all humans were like this one there'd have been no war to call off
line: If every human were like you, I'd have had no war to call off.

thought: dinner is coming and there's always too much
line: My dinner's on its way. Do stay, Traveller. There's always too much.

thought: trusts them with the secret of the mine
line: Mind the mine stays our secret, won't you, human? Only a few know.

thought: they're poking at the roots again, though the roots are fine
line: Harumph! Do stop poking at the roots. They're quite healthy now.

thought: hopes they left the mine as they found it
line: You did leave the mine as you found it, I hope? Mostly?

thought: killed one demon and has strutted ever since
line: One black demon, and you've been strutting about ever since.

thought: reminds people there's a queue for the gliders
line: Somebody remind our hero there's a queue for the gliders.

thought: Glough warned him about humans, and some days he sees why
line: Glough warned me about humans. Some days I almost see his point.

thought: Daero's recruits train harder than this one has ever walked
line: Daero's recruits train harder than you've ever walked, human.

thought: his dinner is always late when they're about, suspiciously
line: You've eaten my dinner, haven't you? It's always late when you visit.

thought: Glough's treehouse has room, should they outstay their welcome
line: Glough's treehouse has a spare room, should you outstay your welcome.

thought: names the three who died
line: Mekritus, Andiess, Flaygian. I say their names before I sleep.

thought: his own blood was used against his comrades
line: My own blood, used against my own people. I cannot wash that off.

thought: wanted Serafina to be real so badly he stopped thinking
line: Serafina. I wanted her real so badly that I stopped thinking.

thought: Meiyerditch says the Myreque's name aloud now
line: Meiyerditch says our name aloud now. I hardly know what to do with it.

thought: the word in the ghetto is right, for once
line: Word in the ghetto is that Ranis is dead. Word is right, for once.

thought: the power comes and leaves him gaps
line: When the power comes, I lose the minutes after. I wish I didn't.

thought: tides turn back too; he is wary of hope
line: The tide has turned, they say. Tides turn back, too. I remember that.

thought: three empty bunks he can't bring himself to clear
line: Three empty bunks below. I've not had the heart to clear them.

thought: this one killed Ranis Drakan, and the city will tell it
line: You killed Ranis Drakan, my friend. The ghetto will tell it for years.

thought: they came back to the Myreque after Vanstrom's creature
line: You came back to us after Vanstrom's creature. I owe you for that.

thought: people speak of the Myreque openly, and of this one too
line: People here speak of the Myreque out loud now. Of you, too.

thought: something real to hope for, not a myth
line: You gave this city something real to hope for. Not a myth.

thought: would follow them into Castle Drakan, though he'd rather not
line: My friend, I'd follow you into Castle Drakan. Only don't make me.

thought: asks the others to let the tide-turner pass quietly
line: There goes the one who turned the tide. Let them pass, quietly.

thought: a moment's rest is owed, even down here
line: Sit, my friend. You've earned a moment's rest, even down here.

thought: has no words for what they did, and keeps looking
line: I don't have the words for what you did. I'll keep looking.

thought: walked into a Drakan's hall and out; mustn't make a habit of it
line: Into a Drakan's hall and out again. Don't make a habit of it.

thought: killing Ranis doesn't make them immortal
line: My friend, killing Ranis does not make you immortal. Please remember.

thought: every vampyre in the city must know that face now
line: Every vampyre in Meiyerditch must know your face by now. Well done.

thought: suspects they half believed in Serafina too
line: You believed in Serafina too, a little. Don't deny it.

thought: someone ought to remind the tide-turner that walls are for hiding behind
line: Someone remind our tide-turner that walls are for hiding behind.

thought: reckless again, and he's tired of counting them back in
line: Reckless again. I'm too tired to keep counting you back in.

thought: the tide turned and they'd like the credit; they've earned some
line: The tide turned, and you'd like the credit. You've earned some.

thought: he has a power he can't control, they a temper they won't
line: I've a power I can't control. You've a temper you won't. Some pair.

thought: Ivan is with Drezel now, out of harm's way
line: Ivan's at Paterdomus with Drezel. Safer there, and he'll learn.

thought: Drezel will make a priest of the lad, or the lad will wear him out
line: Drezel will make a priest of Ivan yet. Or Ivan will drive him mad.

thought: a rod that freezes vampyres; he'd thought it a story
line: A rod that freezes vampyres. I'd been told it was only a story.

thought: Gadderanks thought the Burgh easy pickings
line: Gadderanks thought the Burgh would be easy pickings. He thought wrong.

thought: named after a swamp, and about as tidy
line: Folk named us after a swamp. Fitting. We're about as tidy.

thought: Safalaan led people out; he feels he only loses them
line: Safalaan got people out of Meiyerditch. I mostly lose them.

thought: asks Saradomin to keep Ivan out of trouble
line: Saradomin, keep Ivan out of trouble. Drezel can only do so much.

thought: one rod against all Morytania is still more than they had
line: One rod against all of Morytania. Still, it's more than we had.

thought: the two of them stood against Gadderanks and his guards
line: You and I against Gadderanks and his guards. I'd do it again.

thought: they brought back a rod that works
line: You brought back a rod that works. I'd stopped hoping it would.

thought: if the Myreque had ranks, they'd get one
line: If the Myreque were organised, I'd give you a rank. We're not.

thought: the Burgh still stands, and they had a hand in it
line: The Burgh's still standing. You had a hand in that, friend.

thought: Saradomin sent them twice; it isn't luck
line: Saradomin sent you twice now. I've stopped calling it luck.

thought: would have made a fine Myreque from the start
line: You'd have made a fine Myreque from the start. Better late, eh?

thought: someone he'd trust with silver and with Ivan
line: There's one I'd trust with silver, and with Ivan.

thought: the Myreque owe them a drink at the least
line: Sit down, friend. The Myreque owe you a drink, at the least.

thought: the rod works; it's not for poking vampyres for fun
line: You got the rod working. Don't go poking vampyres with it for fun.

thought: the Myreque aren't organised enough to have heroes
line: We're not organised enough to have heroes. Don't start.

thought: keep stories away from Ivan; he's trouble enough
line: Keep away from Ivan with your stories. He's trouble enough already.

thought: went hunting a dead hero's rod and came back pleased
line: Went hunting a dead hero's rod and came back pleased as punch.

thought: carry silver; he shouldn't have to say it twice
line: Carry silver, friend. I shouldn't have to tell you twice.

thought: strolling about as if Morytania owes them a favour
line: Look at that one, strolling about like Morytania owes them a favour.

thought: Gadderanks answered to someone worse; no time to look pleased
line: Don't look so pleased. Gadderanks answered to someone worse.

thought: would make a decent Myreque if they ever learned to whisper
line: You'd make a decent Myreque, if you ever learned to whisper.

thought: brown suited Grubfoot, and on a bigger goblin it suits better
line: Brown look good on Grubfoot. Look better on me. Bigger.

thought: Bentnoze is claiming the brown idea, which is wrong, as always
line: Brown my idea. Bentnoze say his idea. Bentnoze wrong, like always.

thought: keeping one bit of green back, in case
line: Me keep one green armour, hid. Just in case brown go wrong.

thought: he said he could do peace if it wore green; it wears brown, and he copes
line: Peace now. Brown peace. Not green, but me manage.

thought: everyone in the hut is bored now, even the one nobody listens to
line: Bentnoze bored. Me bored. Even Grubfoot bored, and him not allowed.

thought: the next argument is already lining up
line: Armour done. Now me want battleaxes, Bentnoze want hammers. Again.

thought: brown reminds him of mud, and mud of soggy things he likes
line: Brown like mud. Like soggy mud. Me like soggy.

thought: decides the war god would approve of an earthy colour
line: Big High War God like brown, me think. Earthy. Like battlefield.

thought: the human held up the brown, and he pictured himself in it
line: Human hold up brown, and me see me in it. Very handsome.

thought: the human stopped Bentnoze shouting red all day
line: Bentnoze stop shouting red, thanks to human. Best day in hut.

thought: goblins are poor at peace, and the human made some anyway
line: Human make peace in general hut. Goblins never manage that.

thought: three lots of armour fetched and not one complaint
line: Human fetch armour three time. Not one moan. Good goblin, nearly.

thought: greets the human the old tribal way, to annoy Bentnoze
line: Me give human tribal bow. Old way. Bentnoze can sulk.

thought: the war god made humans stupid, but this one slipped past
line: Big High War God make humans stupid. This one got missed.

thought: orders Grubfoot to fetch the human a treat
line: Grubfoot! Get this one juicy maggot. Earned it.

thought: the human may stand in the hut now, just on the right side
line: Human welcome in hut now. Not on Bentnoze side, though.

thought: blue was the worst idea he has ever seen on a goblin
line: Human bring blue! Blue! Goblin in blue look like sad fish.

thought: all that searching to end at the colour of mud
line: Human take whole day to find brown. Brown! Mud brown!

thought: the job is done, and now the human is just ugly in his hut
line: Armour done, human. Now human just ugly thing in hut.

thought: brown was his idea; the human was only the legs
line: Brown me idea. Human just legs that carry it.

thought: can still see the orange when he shuts his eyes
line: Orange, human! Me still see orange when me shut eyes.

thought: with peace made there's nothing to shout at but Bentnoze
line: Human make peace. Now nobody to shout at but Bentnoze. Thanks.

thought: suspects the human knows where the spare armour crates are
line: Grubfoot, count crates. That one know where spare armour live.

thought: the human helped Bentnoze too, and now smells of his dinner
line: Human help Bentnoze too? Ugh. Human smell of beetle pie now.
